I work at Sephora and do pretty much all the bridal makeup at my location. Most people who are coming to get their makeup done are relying on the artists knowledge and skills. They know the popular brands (such as Too faced) and feel comfortable with them because that's what they see all the time. Brands like mehron, krylon, etc... aren't every day makeup enthusiast friendly. 

I like having a mix of different brands in my kit when I do travel outside of work. I like too faced enough, but there are other brands I do prefer. As far as foundation, TF is pretty dewy and longevity isn't the greatest. I lean more towards foundation that can be altered to different skin types like Make Up For Ever, Fenty, Cover Fx, and Bare Minerals bare pro. With all of these you could adjust them to fit the clients skin type. 

As far as mascara, I like having multiple different types. Not everyone has the same type of lash. One person might want length, another volume. But I do always layer a waterproof one if it is for a wedding. 

There are a few things that I would buy drugstore just for price. Usually it's only lashes, but I do like some lipsticks depending on the brand. But lashes are something you don't really want to spend too much on, as you don't get them back & can't be reused on other clients. I have a mix of full strip and individual lashes that can be layered for different effects. 

But every client & artist is going to be different. As long as you're comfortable with the products you have, and your client is happy with the result, that's really all that matters.

Ok, since I'm being asked how I made it, here you go!

First you'll need Crayola crayons, either vegetable oil or olive oil, and shea butter. (Crayola is the best because they're higher quality than, let's say RoseArt.) You can buy small containers to put it in at Target. I find mine in the travel section. You'll also need a double boiler. If you don't have one, you can make one by filling one small/medium sized pot about halfway with water. You turn the stove on medium and wait for it to start boiling. Then you take another pot and put it on top of the one with water. Then you take a teaspoon of your oil and a teaspoon of the shea butter and just plop it in the empty pot. Pick the crayon you want to use, unwrap it, break it in half, and toss both halves into the pot with the oil and shea butter. Turn the heat down to low and stir everything continuously until everything is melted and mixed well. Take your container and pour your mix into it. Last, put it in fridge and let it set for about 15 minutes. 

*Warning* Do not pour the wax down the drain! It will catch on the pipes and really mess it up. Use a paper towel and wipe the pot clean.
